title: Masking-rate map: per-field versus linear masking rate on the 84-field model, and where our code departs from MD4 and LLaDA
headline: Do the papers' masking settings beat ours on the 84-field model?
setup: Our model writes a team of six Pokémon as 84 fields, such as a species or a move. Two published papers, MD4 and LLaDA, train and sample such models differently from us. This map asks whether their settings do better. A row is one way to train and sample the model, and four are compared.
alt: Nothing has run yet. Three tickets are closed and the code ticket is next. Four rows are compared, two trainings and nine grids will answer, and a row wins when its error is at least 0.001 lower at two or more guidance values.
terms: The chance a field is hidden in training. Per-field, ours: species are almost never hidden. Linear, the papers': every field has the same chance
One way to train and sample the model. Four are compared. The control is Per-field, uncorrected t: our own settings
The t at which training hid as many fields as are still hidden at this pass
Measures how far the model's choices move when told the corrected t: 0 is no change. Under 0.01, the correction cannot matter, and the row is not battled
One battled run of a row at one guidance value: teams sampled at 23 asks, each team battled 49 times
How far the win rate the teams get is from the win rate asked for. Lower is better. A row must be 0.001 lower to count
How hard the sampler pushes toward the win rate asked for. 1 is no push, and higher pushes harder

frames.title: 1. Where the map stands: the code ticket is next
frames.takes: Three tickets are closed and the code ticket is next, before any training.
frames.measured: No training or battle has run; the three closed tickets only fixed the plan.

frames.title: 2. Four rows: masking rate by decoding setting
frames.takes: Four rows: two masking rates, each with two ways of decoding. Per-field, corrected t is battled only if the t check says so.
frames.expected: Linear, species-first matches the control within training luck. Linear, random order loses to it.
frames.surprise: A linear row wins by 0.002 or more.

frames.title: 3. The cost: one table, two trainings, nine grids
frames.takes: Both trainings read one table, then nine grids are battled.
frames.measured: Two trainings of about 6.7 hours each, then 1.95 million battles, about 6.9 hours.

frames.title: 4. What a win looks like

left.title: A win
lines: Error at least 0.001 lower than the control
At two or more of guidance 2, 4 and 8

right.title: Reported as a trade
lines: A win whose pooled win rate falls by more than 0.026

frames.takes: A row wins when its error is clearly lower at two or more guidance values.
frames.expected: Linear, species-first matches the control, and no row wins.
frames.surprise: A linear row wins at all three guidance values.
